cds.text: Understand that texts take many forms, such as signs, books and digital texts
Explore how texts are organised by purpose, such as to recount, narrate, express opinion, inform, report and explain
Identify how curriculum texts are organised differently and use language features depending on purpose
Understand conventions of print and screen, including how books and simple digital texts are organised
Explore how repetition, rhyme and rhythm create cohesion in simple poems, chants and songs
Understand how texts are made cohesive through personal and possessive pronouns and omitting inferable words
Understand how print and screen texts use features such as page numbers, contents, headings, titles, navigation buttons, links and images
Navigate print and screen texts using chapters, contents, indexes, side-bar or drop-down menus, and links
Identify familiar texts, such as stories and informative texts, and their purposes
Discuss different texts and identify features that indicate their purposes
Identify how similar topics and information are presented in different text types
Identify some differences between imaginative and informative texts
Describe similarities and differences among imaginative, informative and persuasive texts
Identify the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts
Read decodable and authentic texts using developing phonic knowledge, and monitor meaning using context and emerging grammar
Read decodable and authentic texts with developing phonic knowledge, phrasing and fluency, monitoring meaning with context and grammar
Read texts with phrasing and fluency using phonic and word knowledge, re-reading and self-correcting
Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising and questioning to understand and discuss texts
Use comprehension strategies while listening, viewing and reading to build literal and inferred meaning, using vocabulary, context and text structures
Use comprehension strategies, including monitoring, to build literal and inferred meaning
Recognise and generate rhyming words, alliteration, syllables and phonemes in spoken words (phonological awareness)
Segment words into separate phonemes, including consonant blends or clusters at the beginning and end of words
Manipulate more complex sounds in spoken words, using blending, segmenting, phoneme deletion and substitution to read and write words
Segment sentences into words; blend and segment single-syllable words; isolate, blend and manipulate phonemes
Orally manipulate initial, medial and final phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution to generate new words
Recognise and name upper- and lower-case letters and know the most common sound each letter represents
Read one- and two-syllable words
Use short and common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs to write and blend words; read consonant clusters and silent letters in words of one or more syllables, including compound words
Write CVC words by representing sounds with letters, and blend sounds when reading CVC words
Understand that a letter can represent more than one sound and that every syllable must contain a vowel sound
Use knowledge of letters and sounds to spell words
Spell one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns
Use spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words not fully predictable from sounds, including high-frequency words
Read and write some high-frequency and familiar words
Read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words
Build morphemic word families using knowledge of prefixes and suffixes
Understand that words are units of meaning and can be made of more than one meaningful part
Recognise and use grammatical morphemes to create word families

sentences.text: {{S}} comprehends digital texts and advertisements and identifies key ideas in narratives.
{{S}} identifies main ideas, understands simple inferences and explains how authors use evidence to support ideas.
{{S}} reads with confidence and connects with the ideas in texts.
{{S}} uses background knowledge and reading skills to better understand texts.
{{S}} identifies key ideas and supporting details when reading.
{{S}} can interpret language features, explain how authors use evidence to support ideas and understands simple inferences when reading moderately complex texts.
{{S}} identifies main ideas and is beginning to recognise how language features help build meaning.
{{S}} reads predictable texts with growing confidence and identifies key ideas to support comprehension.
{{S}} reads simple texts with support and is working towards identifying key information and following the main ideas.
{{S}} is beginning to explain how language features, such as word choices and text clues, contribute to meaning.
{{S}} understands simple, predictable texts.
{{S}} reads predictable texts with guidance and draws basic connections to gain a clearer understanding of the stories.
{{S}} reads simple, familiar texts and is building confidence in recognising high-frequency words.
{{S}} comprehends predictable imaginative texts from the main character's perspective.
{{S}} tracks print from left to right.
{{S}} knows the front and back of a book.
{{S}} identifies the spaces between words in a text.
{{S}} hears and says the first, middle and final sounds in familiar spoken words.
{{S}} blends chunks of spoken words to make new words, such as 'talk-ing'.
{{S}} has a strong understanding of taught letters and the sounds they usually make.
{{S}} recognises some taught letters of the alphabet and the sounds they make.
{{S}} participates in whole class reading activities to blend and segment words.
{{S}} listens to familiar stories that are read to {{o}} and recalls basic events that occurred.
{{S}} stops at full stops and changes {{pos}} voice for questions when reading aloud.
{{S}} uses pictures to help {{o}} understand stories that are read to {{o}}.
{{S}} segments and blends words to read decodable texts with improved fluency and comprehension.
{{S}} can identify the beginning and final sound in words.
{{S}} uses background knowledge and personal experiences to connect with texts when reading.
{{S}} self-corrects when {{pos}} fluency or meaning is interrupted.
{{S}} has shown growth in recognising and re-reading when meaning has been interrupted.
{{S}} makes connections between {{pos}} experiences and the events in a story.
{{S}} uses headings, pictures and captions to find information in a text.
{{S}} reads between the lines using clues in the text.
{{S}} reads longer texts with accuracy and uses appropriate volume and speed when reading aloud.
{{S}} uses strategies to fix {{pos}} understanding when meaning breaks down.
{{S}} locates relevant information in a text.
{{S}} identifies how persuasive, informative and imaginative texts are organised.
{{S}} compares print and digital texts to decide which is most useful for a task.
{{S}} engages with texts for different purposes.
{{S}} shows likes and dislikes about a story.
{{S}} recognises familiar words in texts.
{{S}} asks questions when the meaning is unclear.
{{S}} recalls key events and characters in a story.
{{S}} recalls key facts from an information text.

rows.newText: {{S}} recognises that signs, books and screens are different kinds of texts.
{{S}} names different kinds of texts and says what each one is used for.
{{S}} knows that stories are written to entertain and that other texts give information.
{{S}} identifies familiar texts and talks about why they were made.
{{S}} says how a story is different from a text that gives facts.
{{S}} tells the difference between an imaginative text and an informative text.
{{S}} handles books and screens correctly and knows where to begin reading.
{{S}} predicts what might happen next in a story and talks about {{pos}} ideas.
{{S}} uses letter sound knowledge to read simple decodable texts.
{{S}} explains how a recount, a story and an opinion text are put together for their purpose.
{{S}} recognises that a text can be organised to tell, to inform or to share an opinion.
{{S}} enjoys the repetition, rhyme and rhythm in poems, chants and songs.
{{S}} explains how repeated words and rhymes hold a simple poem together.
{{S}} uses contents pages, headings and links to find information in a text.
{{S}} talks about the features of a text that show why it was written.
{{S}} discusses different texts and points out clues that show their purpose.
{{S}} describes how stories, information texts and opinion texts are alike and different.
{{S}} sorts texts into imaginative, informative and persuasive groups and gives reasons.
{{S}} uses visualising, predicting and questioning to understand texts read aloud.
{{S}} reads decodable texts with growing fluency and checks that they make sense.
{{S}} explains how a text is organised differently depending on its purpose.
{{S}} recognises how pronouns make a text flow and avoids repeating nouns.
{{S}} explains how pronouns link ideas from one sentence to the next.
{{S}} navigates print and screen texts using contents pages, indexes, menus and links.
{{S}} compares how the same topic is presented in different kinds of texts.
{{S}} identifies how information about one topic changes between a book and a website.
{{S}} identifies the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts.
{{S}} explains who a text is written for and what the author wants the reader to do or feel.
{{S}} reads aloud with expression and re-reads to check that the meaning is clear.
{{S}} uses comprehension strategies to build both literal and inferred meaning.
